entry.title: Beyond 2030: A Development Agenda Fit for a Changed World
entry.summary:
BERLIN / MUNICH, November 27 (IPS) - The global landscape has changed profoundly since the adoption of the 2030 Agenda in 2015. Rising geopolitical tensions, galloping military expenditures, accelerating technological transformation—including the omnipresence of artificial intelligence (AI) —and mounting pressures on development financing are reshaping national and international priorities. These shifts raise fundamental questions about the relevance, ambition and accountability of the global development agenda beyond 2030, and even its feasibility.

entry.title: Brazil: Democracy Defended from Below
entry.summary:
MONTEVIDEO, Uruguay, November 27 (IPS) - Brazil’s President Lula da Silva owes his fourth term less to his campaign than to the people who mobilised to stop his far-right opponent. Three weeks after losing the first round, the 80-year-old was elected for another term in the 25 October runoff with around 52 per cent of the valid vote. This was the first such comeback since Brazil’s return to democracy. Online activists, students, trade unionists and millions of voters who stayed home for the first round turned the result around by mobilising on the streets, online and at the polls. The question now is whether that mobilisation will last beyond the electoral emergency, and whether it can help Lula push his agenda through a Congress where the right holds the upper hand.

entry.title: Creating Opportunities in the Maritime Transition for Latin America and the Caribbean
entry.summary:
LONDON, November 26 (IPS) - The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye comes at a decisive moment for humanity. We are now grappling with a scenario in which the Paris Agreement goal of limiting global warming to 1.5 °C will not be met, which brings the concept of “overshoot” to the fore. The best current aspiration is to limit the extent of that overshoot, peak emissions as soon as possible, and then return to 1.5 °C.
